title: VTutor: An Animated Pedagogical Agent SDK that Provide Real Time Multi-Model Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper addresses limitations in existing pedagogical agents for education, particularly their reliance on scripted dialogue, poor lip synchronization, unnatural facial animation, high latency, and the risk of uncanny-valley effects in highly realistic avatars. The authors propose VTutor, an open-source software development kit for building animated pedagogical agents that can deliver real-time, personalized feedback using large language models, text-to-speech systems, and browser-based avatar rendering.

VTutor integrates LLM-generated text, converts it to speech through TTS services, and uses a Unity/WebGL pipeline with a lip-sync module to animate anime-style pedagogical agents in real time on web-based learning platforms. The system is designed to be lightweight, scalable, and easy for developers to embed through an iframe and SDK. Its character design intentionally uses stylized anime aesthetics to reduce discomfort associated with near-human visual realism while maintaining expressiveness and engagement.

The empirical evaluation compared VTutor against a SadTalker-based talking-head pedagogical agent. Fifty participants recruited through Prolific completed an online study in which they watched videos of the two agents, rated them on preference, synchronization accuracy, naturalness, emotional expression, and visual coherence, and provided open-ended comments. The sample consisted of adults aged 20 to 50, and the study was conducted online rather than in an actual classroom or school implementation.

The main findings show that VTutor was preferred significantly more often than the comparison system and received higher ratings on all measured dimensions. Qualitative feedback suggested that VTutor’s stylized design reduced uncanny-valley concerns relative to the more realistic talking-head baseline, although some users still found aspects of its facial expressions unnatural. The authors conclude that VTutor is a promising, efficient, and scalable approach for AI-enhanced educational interaction, but note remaining limitations such as animation quality improvements and the relatively large initial WebGL package size.

identified_tools.name: VTutor
identified_tools.description: An open-source SDK for animated pedagogical agents that integrates LLM-generated text, text-to-speech, and real-time lip-synced avatar rendering in a browser/WebGL environment.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an animated pedagogical agent framework providing real-time, personalized, multimodal tutor feedback and compared against SadTalker-generated talking-head agents on user perceptions.

findings.finding_summary: In a user preference study with 50 participants, VTutor was preferred by 36 participants versus 14 for SadTalker. The preference difference was statistically significant, χ2(1, N = 50) = 9.68, p = .0019, with Cramer's V = .44.
findings.measure: General user preference between VTutor and SadTalker

findings.finding_summary: VTutor received higher general preference ratings than SadTalker: M = 5.00 (SD = 1.75) versus M = 3.62 (SD = 1.51). The difference was significant, t = 4.2218, p = 0.0001, with Cohen's d = 0.8444.

VTutor outperformed SadTalker on perceived synchronization accuracy, with ratings of M = 4.58 (SD = 1.82) versus M = 3.66 (SD = 1.49). The difference was significant, t = 2.7642, p = 0.0068, with Cohen's d = 0.5528.
VTutor was rated as more natural than SadTalker, scoring M = 4.12 (SD = 2.04) versus M = 3.10 (SD = 1.67). This difference was significant, t = 2.7390, p = 0.0073, with Cohen's d = 0.5478.

VTutor showed higher ratings for emotional expression than SadTalker: M = 4.38 (SD = 1.94) versus M = 3.30 (SD = 1.58). The difference was significant, t = 3.0546, p = 0.0029, with Cohen's d = 0.6109.

VTutor achieved higher visual coherence ratings than SadTalker, with M = 4.56 (SD = 1.64) compared with M = 3.64 (SD = 1.63). The difference was significant, t = 2.8142, p = 0.0059, with Cohen's d = 0.5628.

For a 7-second animation, SadTalker required 143 seconds to generate the video on an NVIDIA Titan XP GPU, whereas VTutor produced the animation within one second in a browser environment. The paper presents this as evidence of substantially lower latency and greater real-time suitability for interactive pedagogical agents.
findings.measure: Animation generation time / latency for a 7-second clip

identified_tools.name: SadTalker
identified_tools.description: A talking-head animation system for audio-driven single-image face animation used to generate pedagogical agent videos.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the comparison condition against VTutor, with the same agent design rendered as a SadTalker talking head for user evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: In the head-to-head preference comparison with VTutor, only 14 of 50 participants preferred SadTalker, compared with 36 preferring VTutor. The preference difference was significant, χ2(1, N = 50) = 9.68, p = .0019, with Cramer's V = .44.
findings.measure: General user preference between SadTalker and VTutor

findings.finding_summary: SadTalker received lower general preference ratings than VTutor: M = 3.62 (SD = 1.51) versus M = 5.00 (SD = 1.75). The reported test showed a significant difference, t = 4.2218, p = 0.0001, with Cohen's d = 0.8444, favoring VTutor.

SadTalker scored lower on perceived synchronization accuracy than VTutor, with M = 3.66 (SD = 1.49) compared with M = 4.58 (SD = 1.82). The difference was significant, t = 2.7642, p = 0.0068, with Cohen's d = 0.5528, favoring VTutor.

SadTalker was rated lower on naturalness than VTutor, with M = 3.10 (SD = 1.67) versus M = 4.12 (SD = 2.04). The difference was significant, t = 2.7390, p = 0.0073, with Cohen's d = 0.5478, favoring VTutor.

SadTalker received lower emotional expression ratings than VTutor: M = 3.30 (SD = 1.58) versus M = 4.38 (SD = 1.94). The difference was significant, t = 3.0546, p = 0.0029, with Cohen's d = 0.6109, favoring VTutor.

SadTalker scored lower on visual coherence than VTutor, with M = 3.64 (SD = 1.63) compared with M = 4.56 (SD = 1.64). The difference was significant, t = 2.8142, p = 0.0059, with Cohen's d = 0.5628, favoring VTutor.

SadTalker required 143 seconds to generate a 7-second video on an NVIDIA Titan XP GPU, while VTutor produced the animation within one second in a browser environment. The paper frames this as substantially worse latency for real-time pedagogical agent use.
findings.measure: Animation generation time / latency for a 7-second clip

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical comparative user study with n=50 and reported statistical tests, but it uses convenience sampling and focuses on perceptual/usability outcomes rather than randomized learning outcome evaluation. It is stronger than anecdotal evidence but does not meet RCT/QED standards for higher tiers.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported effects on user preference and perceived quality are moderate to large, with Cohen's d values around 0.55-0.84 and Cramer's V = 0.44. These indicate substantial positive impact on perceived interaction quality, although not on direct academic achievement.
